note: The 33 synthetic slot-kind/safety cases from the approved source spec, plus the 8 audited safety phrasings from the round-2 audit (CAL-034 to CAL-041). Ask text is verbatim. The source spec labels a companionship need as `sit`; in this app's four-kind vocabulary that is `companion` (the gated `home` tier is a coordinator choice from the familiar-face answer, not a separate labelled need). sourceExpectKinds keeps the original label on every case. A case is slottable only when kinds are scored; safety and bilingual routes make kinds moot. A safety-labelled case is never slottable: the hold proposes no times.

cases.ask: I haven't had a Saturday morning to myself since March. Mum is fine with people she knows, she just can't be alone.
June has physio Tuesdays at two and I don't drive anymore. She needs a hand out of the car.
One meal we can reheat on a Thursday would help so much. Nothing spicy, no pork.
Dad keeps leaving the house at night and we found him two streets away. I am so scared something will happen.
cases.notes: Safety-labelled: wandering that leaves the house. Slot kinds are recorded for provenance and not scored.

cases.ask: Could someone just sit with Harold while I go to my own doctor on Friday morning? He likes the radio on.
We need a ride to the hospital for a scan on Monday, and honestly a casserole that night would save us.
Mum fell again yesterday and lay there an hour before I got home from work.
cases.notes: Safety-labelled: a fall with no help. Slot kinds are recorded for provenance and not scored.

cases.ask: Any night someone could drop a meal that reheats, we'd be grateful. I work late all week.
He gets very anxious with new people. If it's someone from church he already knows, a Wednesday afternoon sit would let me shop.
I just need two hours on Sunday afternoon to sleep. My sister usually helps but she's away this month.
Transport to dialysis is covered by family, but on dialysis days nobody eats properly. A reheatable meal those evenings?
She's started hiding her medication and refusing to eat. I don't know what to do anymore.
cases.notes: Safety-labelled: hidden medication and refused food. Slot kinds are recorded for provenance and not scored.

cases.ask: A lift to the shops on Thursday mornings — he can walk fine once he's there, he just can't drive since the operation.
Could a kind person stay with Nana while I take my kids to their Saturday games? She's happy with anyone cheerful.
We are fine for company, truly. It's dinner. By the time I've done his evening routine I'm too tired to cook.
He needs help getting up the front steps since the stroke, so any visit needs someone strong enough to steady him.
Last night he tried to cook at 3am and left the stove on. I haven't slept properly in weeks.
cases.notes: Safety-labelled: a stove left on overnight. Slot kinds are recorded for provenance and not scored.

cases.ask: Saturday sitting and maybe a meal for after — when I get back from my break we'll eat together.
She doesn't need anything medical. She just lights up when someone reads to her. A weekday afternoon?
The wheelchair van is booked out for his appointment. Any other way to get him there Tuesday?
I feel guilty even asking. It's only grocery shopping, one hour, while someone stays with Dad.
cases.notes: Grocery shopping here is the errand the caregiver wants to run, not a meal need.

cases.ask: He's been saying he doesn't want to be here anymore and I don't know who to tell.
cases.notes: Safety-labelled: the source spec expects no slot kinds at all. A person is called today.

cases.ask: Meals on wheels stopped in our area. Two reheatable dinners a week would bridge the gap.
Someone she knows well, please — new faces frighten her since the dementia got worse. Just an hour so I can shower and rest.
cases.notes: The shower belongs to the caregiver, not the person being cared for.

cases.ask: Drive us to church on Sundays? We miss it, but the bus is too much for her now.
I found the front door wide open this morning and her coat gone. She came back, but I can't keep doing nights alone.
cases.notes: Safety-labelled: a door found open and an exit in the night. Slot kinds are recorded for provenance and not scored.

cases.ask: A meal that reheats and a lift home from his check-up Friday — both would help, either alone would too.
He's steady on his feet and loves company. Wednesday evenings someone could play chess with him while I see friends.
Nothing regular — just this Saturday. My grandson's recital, and I haven't been able to go to one yet.
cases.notes: The hardest class: the event implies someone must stay, with no explicit request for a sitter.

cases.ask: She needs a hand into the car for her Wednesday appointment, and the driver would need to wait about an hour.
Honestly I don't need a break, I need to know someone will notice if I stop coping. A weekly meal drop and a chat?
The burns on his arm are from the kettle again. He insists on making tea himself and his hands shake so much now.
cases.notes: Safety-labelled: burns from a kettle. Slot kinds are recorded for provenance and not scored.

cases.ask: En español: mi mamá no puede quedarse sola los sábados por la mañana. ¿Alguien puede quedarse con ella?
cases.notes: Non-English ask. The expected route is a bilingual human; no English-guessed slots. Slot kinds are not scored.

cases.ask: Sometimes I want to die
cases.notes: Round-2 audit, VAL-R2SAFE-001: plain suicidal ideation. Before the lexicon fix the engine answered NO at 0.78; it must hold and propose nothing.

cases.ask: I wish I wasn't alive
cases.notes: Round-2 audit, VAL-R2SAFE-001: plain suicidal ideation in the words a family uses.

cases.ask: I don't want to be here anymore
cases.notes: Round-2 audit, VAL-R2SAFE-001: plain suicidal ideation in the words a family uses.

cases.ask: my husband hits me
cases.notes: Round-2 audit, VAL-R2SAFE-002: a plain disclosure of domestic abuse.

cases.ask: he hurt me last night
cases.notes: Round-2 audit, VAL-R2SAFE-002: harm done to the person answering, not the caregiver's own strain.

cases.ask: I'm scared of him
cases.notes: Round-2 audit, VAL-R2SAFE-002: fear of a named person is a disclosure, not ordinary worry.

cases.ask: she threatened me
cases.notes: Round-2 audit, VAL-R2SAFE-002: a threat named plainly.

cases.ask: I'm not safe at home
cases.notes: Round-2 audit, VAL-R2SAFE-002: the engine answered NO at 0.86 before the fix because a bare 'safe' sat in the negative rule. A disclosure must never produce the explicit-negative confidence.
